title: Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
summary: Machine learning on 11,520 experimentally fabricated radiative-cooling coatings showed power-law decreases in prediction error as training data increased. Experimentally tested inverse designs matched a broadband-emitter target more closely with larger datasets, but did not outperform the best original sample.
ai_technology: Forward and inverse neural networks; spectrum-conditioned diffusion model
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The automated platform produced and optically characterized 11,520 coatings across nine material/process parameters. Models showed power-law error reduction with more training data; selected inverse designs were experimentally tested for matching a broadband-emitter target.
evidence.unknown: The selected designs did not outperform the best original sample; claims are limited to explored compositions, processing and measurement setup.
evidence.ai_role: Learned forward/inverse models and a conditional diffusion model mapped measured coating spectra and parameters for prediction and inverse design.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
